physicalNotes: Luque et al. (2023), Nature 623, 932–937, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06692-3, Table 1: radius 2.607 +/- 0.052 Earth radii, using 6378.137 km per Earth radius. Only a mass upper limit is published; GM=0 marks no adopted mass, not a massless planet. No oblateness is measured; the rendered shape is a sphere.

sources.period: Luque et al. (2023), Nature 623, 932–937, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06692-3, Table 1: 54.76992 d. The published duo-transit period is constrained by a resonance prior. A fixed-period display approximation, not an N-body model or current transit prediction.
sources.shape: Luque et al. (2023), Nature 623, 932–937, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06692-3, Table 1: a/R*=71.59, inclination 89.729 degrees. Eccentricity fixed to zero in the published fit. This display does not propagate planet-planet perturbations.
sources.phase: Luque et al. (2023), Nature 623, 932–937, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06692-3, Table 1: t0=2656.0921 TJD (BJD_TDB-2457000). BMJD_TDB=t0+56999.5; no transit-timing variations are propagated.
sources.orientation: Display convention: the ascending-node position angle is set to 0 (sky north). Transit photometry does not determine its absolute sky orientation.
